affected_projects.from: New or expanded stand-alone data center or battery energy storage system land-use applications submitted after July 27, 2026; does not affect applications already under review.
affected_projects.to: New or expanded data centers and battery energy storage systems as primary uses, as defined by Resolution No. 2932, including qualifying uses that are not stand-alone. Applications submitted before the moratorium may continue.
affected_projects.reason: The signed resolution defines primary use by several site-level criteria; stand-alone is too narrow.

current_status.from: Active as of the July 31, 2026 research date. Effective immediately upon adoption, the resolution bars submission, acceptance, processing, or approval of new land-use applications for new or expanded data centers or battery energy storage systems as primary uses. Applications already under review are not affected. Runs 120 days (to approximately 2026-11-24) absent extension or repeal, with council review required before expiration.
current_status.to: Resolution 2932 defines primary use by alternative site-level floor-area, construction-cost and electrical-capacity criteria; a site may have multiple primary uses. The city says pre-moratorium applications may continue. This corrects the overly narrow stand-alone description; actual later extensions/repeal and legal force remain unresolved. evidence.supports: Multiple primary uses possible; any one alternative threshold suffices: over 20 percent of gross area, original construction cost, electrical service, or over 20 MW electrical service.
evidence.quote:
C. “Primary use” means an activity or combination of activities of chief importance on a

site and which is one of the main purposes for which the land or structures are intended,

designed, or ordinarily used. A site may have more than one primary use. For purposes of

determining whether a use is a primary use on a site, such use shall be considered primary

if it meets any of the following criteria:

1. The use occupies more than twenty percent (20%) of the total gross square footage

of all buildings and structures on the site;

2. The use accounts for more than twenty percent (20%) of the original construction

cost of all real and personal property on the site; or

3. The use draws more than twenty percent (20%) of the site’s total contracted or

available electrical service capacity, or exceeds 20 megawatts (MW) of contracted

or available capacity
Projects that submitted applications before the moratorium may continue to develop.

decisions.notes: Corrects historical instrument scope; the July source is not independent confirmation of current force. Later repeal or extension was not resolved.

legal_basis.from: Moratorium ordinance adopted by the Woodburn City Council on 2026-09-14; the city filed the required 45-day notice of intent to consider a moratorium with the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development on 2026-07-30 before the council could act.
legal_basis.to: Resolution No. 2267, adopted by Woodburn City Council on September 14, 2026 under ORS 197.505–540. The city filed a 45-day notice with the Oregon Department of Land Conservation and Development.
legal_basis.reason: The city identifies Resolution 2267 rather than an ordinance, and filed a notice.

current_status.from: Active as of 2026-09-23. Moratorium prevents city planning staff from considering any new data center land-use application, effective 2026-09-14 through 2027-01-12. Adopted after the city learned that data center developer Verrus (which had separately applied to build in Salem, where its application drew significant public resistance) was exploring development of a data center on a 237-acre privately owned Southwest Industrial Reserve Area parcel brought into Woodburn's urban growth boundary in 2025; Woodburn had not received a formal application as of adoption. The city separately adopted an ordinance in June 2026 designating data centers as a conditional use in that industrial reserve area, and has hired a consultant (Thomas Consulting Group) to help review and potentially revise its development code for data centers.
